newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian Socialists ignore president's appeal.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian Socialists ignore president's appeal.

text.p: Bulgaria's ex-communist Socialist Party announced on Tuesday that it would form a new government, ignoring an appeal by President Petar Stoyanov for it to yield to opposition demands for a general election.

Interior Minister Nikolai Dobrev, the Socialists' nominee for premier, said he had sympathy for daily mass protest rallies and planned a cabinet of non-party technocrats to bring the country out of severe economic crisis.

"I extend my hand to all Bulgarians, to all political forces, and I insist that together we should work out an anti-crisis programme," said Dobrev, who was jeered by about 100 protesters outside the presidency.
Stoyanov, who took office last Wednesday, had tried to mediate a compromise between the Socialists and the opposition but found no common ground.

Under the constitution, he was obliged to ask the Socialists as the biggest party in parliament to form a cabinet, but on Monday he appealed to them to refuse the mandate and agree to opposition demands for early elections.

"I hope they realise their huge responsibility if they carry out a mandate to form a cabinet which is already rejected by society," Yordan Sokolov, parliamentary leader of the main opposition Union of Democratic Forces told reporters.
The opposition holds Dobrev responsible for clashes between demonstrators and police after protesters besieged and ransacked parliament on January 10.
Opposition leaders have threatened nationwide protests and strikes if the Socialists form a new government, which will be Bulgaria's ninth since the end of one-party rule in 1989.
The Socialists have promised elections by December, a year ahead of schedule. The party leadership was meeting on Tuesday to discuss Dobrev's programme.

Dobrev has a week to name his cabinet, which must be voted on by parliament. The opposition is pinning its hopes on defections from the divided ruling party, which has 125 seats in the 240-seat legislature.
Nationwide rallies were expected later on Tuesday, the 23rd consecutive day of protests against deepening economic crisis blamed on the past two years of Socialist rule.

The collapsing currency slipped below 1,000 lev to the dollar on the interbank market for the first time. But the finance ministry said it had made the twice-yearly interest payment on its Brady bonds, averting a debt default for now.

The Socialists' youth wing said it planned a counter-demonstration on Friday outside the headquarters of the main opposition Union of Democratic Forces in Sofia to protest at what organisers describe as "UDF manipulation".
"I think that the Socialists are clearly looking for a clash but they will not get one on Friday," said student protest organiser Borislav Borislavov.
He said the students would respond by holding their daily rally outside the Socialist headquarters on Friday.
